classification: NOT A BROKEN ELEMENT — A DELIBERATE LEGACY BRIDGE FAMILY. All 18 room verbs declare `affectedStores: []` and forward a @pryzm/command-registry command through `window.commandManager`; the authoritative record lives in the room-topology RoomStore, never in the plugin's SDK RoomsState. That is the stated L-75 / L-79 resolution (plugins/rooms/src/store.ts:11-45, plugins/rooms/src/handlers/legacyCommands.ts §ROOM-ONE-LEGACY-SEAM). Scoring the empty plugin DTO store as a failure would be reading the design as a defect. ⚠ BUT the brief's premise 'rooms is kind=view and derived, not tool-created' is REFUTED: rooms ARE tool-created — apps/editor/src/engine/views/plantools/RoomPlanToolHandler.ts:114 dispatches room.create with a complete RoomData from a user-drawn polygon, and RoomTool (@pryzm/room-topology, instantiated at initTools.ts:3201) is the 3-D equivalent. Derivation (room.redetect) is the DOMINANT path, not the only one.

registration.storeKey_matches_ctx_stores_key: VACUOUSLY — and that is the point. Every room handler declares `affectedStores: []`, so CommandBus.buildContext never resolves a room store key and the mismatch is unrepresentable today. The moment any room handler declares `affectedStores: ['room']` it throws "required store 'room' is missing from HandlerContext.stores" — which is EXACTLY what §FIX-ROOM-CREATE-STORE-KEY had to undo for room.create, the last of eleven siblings to be holding it.

c11_ss11_crosscheck.detail: (1) 'N/A (room derived, not tool-created)' — FALSE, twice over. RoomPlanToolHandler.ts:114 is a USER-DRAWN room polygon dispatching room.create, and CreateRoom.ts's own header names it 'the plan-view room tool's SOLE creation path'; RoomTool.ts:224/387 is the 3-D equivalent. §11.11 states it more carefully ('room.create exists for explicit creation but the dominant path is auto-detection'), so the MATRIX is again the wrong half of its own contract. (2) 'Plan-view tracked ✅ indirect' — FALSE as written: 'room' is NOT in GEOMETRY_ELEMENT_TYPES and every room storeEventBus event is dropped at ViewDependencyTracker.ts:676. Room fills reach the canvas by a DIRECT store read on paint, which is a different mechanism with a different failure mode; '✅ indirect' hides exactly the invalidation gap that matters. (3) 'CEB case ✅ room.create' — TRUE that a case exists, but the column header says 'CEB case (geometry-complete)' and the payload is levelId-only, so the ✅ overstates it; check-mirror-reachability.ts uses room.create as its ORPHAN-CHANNEL CONTROL because nobody subscribes to room.created. CONFIRMED: 'Via RoomStore' and 'Derived — redetected from walls/slabs' are both true as far as they go.

`room.created` is emitted by the CommandEventBridge and subscribed by nobody — check-mirror-reachability.ts uses it as its NEGATIVE CONTROL for exactly that reason. findings.class: P4 / C14 LP-01 — literal (window as any) in an L2 package
findings.claim: packages/room-topology/src/RoomTool.ts:387 fires `(window as any).runtime.bus.executeCommand('room.create', {})` as telemetry. Two separate issues: the literal `(window as any)` double cast in a package (P4), and the `.catch(() => {})` that swallows whatever comes back. The SECOND issue is harmless here ONLY because CreateRoomHandler refuses `{}` by name and takes no undo slot — the same telemetry pattern on furniture and plumbing mints ghost records (B4-FURN-03 / B4-PLUMB-03). Room is the worked example of why validating the create verb is what makes the telemetry shot safe.
findings.contract_clause: P4 (no `(window as any)` outside the allowlisted shim); C14 LP-01. check-cast-count.ts absorbs it in the repo-wide baseline (RC=0 at 100/100), so it is baselined debt, not a new breach.
